aiTitle: Backup production data and test mobile/desktop releases

content.text: I'll start by understanding the release process and current repo state before planning this out — there's real blast radius here (production release channel, merging to main, overwriting "latest").

content.content:
1	# Releasing — versioning & CI
2	
3	Desktop (macOS Tauri app, auto-updates in-app) and mobile (React Native /
4	Expo) releases are **tag-driven** and intentionally separate.
5	
6	- The **git tag is the release trigger and the source of truth for the version.**
7	  You don't have to commit a version bump — tagging *is* the release. CI reads the
8	  version out of the tag and writes it into the app config before building. (The
9	  version committed in the repo is just the dev baseline.)
10	- See also: [DESKTOP_AUTO_UPDATE.md](./DESKTOP_AUTO_UPDATE.md) for the desktop
11	  updater internals, and [UPDATER_KEY_ROTATION.md](./UPDATER_KEY_ROTATION.md)
12	  for generating or rotating the signing key.
13	- For future Mac App Store / TestFlight releases, see
14	  [MACOS_APP_STORE_TESTFLIGHT.md](./MACOS_APP_STORE_TESTFLIGHT.md).
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Versioning model
19	
20	**Separate tag namespaces.** Desktop and mobile can move independently:
21	
22	```
23	desktop-v0.5.0   desktop 0.5.0
24	mobile-v0.2.0    mobile 0.2.0
25	desktop-v0.5.1   desktop 0.5.1
26	```
27	
28	> Why GitHub's *latest* release matters for the updater: the desktop updater
29	> reads `…/releases/latest/download/latest.json`, so the desktop release must be
30	> marked as GitHub's latest release. The desktop workflow forces the `latest`
31	> flag on every desktop release. Mobile releases are also listed on GitHub,
32	> but are explicitly prevented from replacing the latest desktop release.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## 2. How to cut a desktop release
37	
38	### Option A — push a tag (normal path)
39	
40	```bash
41	git checkout main && git pull          # release from main
42	npm version 0.5.0 --no-git-tag-version  # optional: keep repo baseline in sync
43	git commit -am "Release 0.5.0" || true
44	
45	git tag desktop-v0.5.0
46	git push origin desktop-v0.5.0
47	```
48	
49	CI ([`.github/workflows/release.yml`](../.github/workflows/release.yml)) builds
50	the `.dmg` + updater artifacts and publishes the GitHub Release.
51	
52	### Option B — manual run (no tag)
53	
54	Actions tab → **Desktop Release** → **Run workflow** → enter the version.
55	Useful for re-running a failed build.
56	
57	### Option C — build locally
58	
59	CI is not rationed here: `oogxdd/type` is public, and GitHub Actions is free on
60	standard runners for public repositories. Build locally for *speed*, not cost —
61	a cold CI build takes 8–10 minutes, while your Mac rebuilds incrementally in
62	about two:
63	
64	```bash
65	# desktop needs the updater signing key in the environment:
66	export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$(cat ~/.tauri/type-updater.key)"
67	export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="<password>"
68	
69	apps/desktop/scripts/release-local.sh 0.5.0
70	```
71	
72	It bumps the version, builds, signs, assembles `latest.json`, and creates the
73	GitHub Release via `gh` — exactly what CI does. (`gh auth login` required once.)
74	
75	---
76	
77	## 2b. Developing locally without touching the installed prod app
78	
79	The released app and a local dev build are **fully separate installs with
80	separate data**, as long as you use the dev config. Never point a dev run at the
81	production identifier — `com.digital.type2`'s app-data directory is where the
82	real notes live.
83	
84	| | Production | Dev |
85	| --- | --- | --- |
86	| Bundle | `/Applications/Type.app` | `/Applications/Type Dev.app` |
87	| Identifier | `com.digital.type2` | `com.digital.type2.dev` |
88	| App data (notes, profiles, keys) | `~/Library/Application Support/com.digital.type2` | `~/Library/Application Support/com.digital.type2.dev` |
89	| Auto-update | on (GitHub `latest.json`) | off (`endpoints: []`) |
90	
91	Everything above the identifier line is driven by
92	`apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.dev.conf.json`, which Tauri deep-merges over
93	`tauri.conf.json`.
94	
95	```bash
96	npm run desktop:app       # dev run against the dev identifier — safe
97	npm run desktop:dmg:dev   # "Type Dev.dmg", installs alongside prod
98	```
99	
100	`npm run desktop:app:prod-data` exists as an explicit escape hatch: it runs the
101	dev build against the **production** app-data directory. Use it only when you
102	deliberately need to reproduce something against real notes, and back up first
103	(see below).
104	
105	The dev config sets `plugins.updater.endpoints: []`, so a dev build can never
106	download and overwrite itself with a production release. The updater errors with
107	`EmptyEndpoints` if you press "Check for updates" there — that is intended.
108	
109	### Backing up production data
110	
111	Everything the desktop app owns lives under one directory:
112	
113	```bash
114	STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
115	rsync -aH --exclude 'whisper/' --exclude '.DS_Store' \
116	  "$HOME/Library/Application Support/com.digital.type2/" \
117	  "/Volumes/KINGSTON/Backups/type/prod-$STAMP/app-data/"
118	ditto /Applications/Type.app "/Volumes/KINGSTON/Backups/type/prod-$STAMP/Type.app"
119	```
120	
121	`whisper/` is excluded because the managed Python env re-provisions itself.
122	Everything that matters — `notes/`, `profiles/`, `config.json`,
123	`.notes-profiles.json`, `local_sync/` — is a few tens of MB.
124	
125	---
126	
127	## 3. How to cut a mobile release
128	
129	For the native Xcode build and direct App Store Connect upload used by the
130	GitHub-hosted macOS runner, see
131	[MOBILE_TESTFLIGHT_GITHUB_ACTIONS_NATIVE.md](./MOBILE_TESTFLIGHT_GITHUB_ACTIONS_NATIVE.md).
132	
133	```bash
134	git checkout main && git pull
135	git tag mobile-v0.2.0
136	git push origin mobile-v0.2.0
137	```
138	
139	CI ([`.github/workflows/mobile-testflight.yml`](../.github/workflows/mobile-testflight.yml)):
140	
141	1. creates a metadata-only GitHub Release without changing the desktop Latest,
142	2. runs on a macOS runner,
143	3. generates the iOS UniFFI/native module from `packages/mobile-core`,
144	4. archives and exports an `.ipa` with Xcode, and
145	5. validates and uploads that `.ipa` directly to App Store Connect/TestFlight.
146	
147	The workflow sets `MOBILE_VERSION` from the tag and uses the GitHub run number
148	as `IOS_BUILD_NUMBER`. For a manual rerun, use Actions → **Mobile TestFlight**
149	and optionally enter an explicit build number. Manual dispatch uploads a new
150	TestFlight build but does not create a GitHub Release; the `github-release` job
151	runs only for a pushed `mobile-v*` tag. A GitHub Release is version/tag-level,
152	not one-per-TestFlight-build-number.
153	
154	---
155	
156	## 4. Required GitHub secrets
157	
158	Add under **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**.
159	
160	### Mobile (required)
161	
162	The `ios` job uses the `testflight` GitHub Environment. Add the following as
163	environment secrets (or repository secrets if environment scoping is not
164	desired):
165	
166	| Secret | What it is |
167	| --- | --- |
168	| `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | Apple Developer team ID |
169	| `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID` | Team App Store Connect API key ID |
170	| `APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID` | Team App Store Connect API issuer ID |
171	| `APP_STORE_CONNECT_PRIVATE_KEY` | Complete contents of the API key `.p8` file |
172	
173	The runner creates an unsigned intermediate archive, then Xcode uses the team
174	API key and cloud-managed signing to export the signed IPA. A distribution
175	`.p12`, temporary Keychain, `EXPO_TOKEN`, and EAS-managed credentials are not
176	used by the native workflow.
177	See [MOBILE_TESTFLIGHT_GITHUB_ACTIONS_NATIVE.md](./MOBILE_TESTFLIGHT_GITHUB_ACTIONS_NATIVE.md)
178	for the one-time Apple and GitHub setup.
179	
180	### Desktop (required)
181	
182	| Secret                                | What it is                                            |
183	| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
184	| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`           | Contents of `~/.tauri/type-updater.key`               |
185	| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD`  | Password for that key                                 |
186	
187	`GITHUB_TOKEN` is provided automatically (used to create the Release).
188	
189	### Desktop — Apple notarization (optional)
190	
191	Without these the `.dmg` still works but triggers the "unidentified developer"
192	warning on first open. With them, tauri-action notarizes automatically:
193	`APPLE_CERTIFICATE`, `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`,
194	`APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID`.
195	
196	Set **all six or none** — a partially configured setup fails the release rather
197	than falling back to unsigned. Full walkthrough, including the microphone
198	entitlement the hardened runtime requires:
199	[MACOS_CODE_SIGNING.md](./MACOS_CODE_SIGNING.md).
200	
201	---

203	## 5. First-release checklist (one-time)

206	   [DESKTOP_AUTO_UPDATE.md](./DESKTOP_AUTO_UPDATE.md).

236	actually costs is wall-clock time and a little noise.
237	
238	Documentation-only changes are skipped declaratively via `paths-ignore` in
239	`ci.yml`, so there is nothing to remember per commit. The filter skips a run
240	only when **every** changed path matches, so a commit mixing docs and code still
241	runs — it fails in the safe direction.
242	
243	`[skip ci]` (or `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`) in a commit message
244	still works as a manual override. Avoid it for code changes: an opt-out you have
245	to remember gets forgotten exactly when you're in a hurry, which is when CI is
246	worth most.
247	
248	> **The marker is matched as a plain substring, anywhere in the message —
249	> including the body, and including inside backticks or a quotation.** Writing

262	   per-platform, so CI produces nothing the release job could restore. This is
263	   the dominant reason.

265	   Actions restores from the current ref's scope, falling back to the default
266	   branch — so `main → tag` can work, but a cache *saved* under one tag is
267	   invisible to the next tag. Tag-to-tag reuse never happens.
268	3. **Different profiles.** `cargo test --workspace --lib` builds `debug`;

325

# Releasing — versioning & CI

Desktop (macOS Tauri app, auto-updates in-app) and mobile (React Native /
Expo) releases are **tag-driven** and intentionally separate.

- The **git tag is the release trigger and the source of truth for the version.**
  You don't have to commit a version bump — tagging *is* the release. CI reads the
  version out of the tag and writes it into the app config before building. (The
  version committed in the repo is just the dev baseline.)
- See also: [DESKTOP_AUTO_UPDATE.md](./DESKTOP_AUTO_UPDATE.md) for the desktop
  updater internals, and [UPDATER_KEY_ROTATION.md](./UPDATER_KEY_ROTATION.md)
  for generating or rotating the signing key.
- For future Mac App Store / TestFlight releases, see
  [MACOS_APP_STORE_TESTFLIGHT.md](./MACOS_APP_STORE_TESTFLIGHT.md).

---

## 1. Versioning model

**Separate tag namespaces.** Desktop and mobile can move independently:

```
desktop-v0.5.0   desktop 0.5.0
mobile-v0.2.0    mobile 0.2.0
desktop-v0.5.1   desktop 0.5.1
```

> Why GitHub's *latest* release matters for the updater: the desktop updater
> reads `…/releases/latest/download/latest.json`, so the desktop release must be
> marked as GitHub's latest release. The desktop workflow forces the `latest`
> flag on every desktop release. Mobile releases are also listed on GitHub,
> but are explicitly prevented from replacing the latest desktop release.

---

## 2. How to cut a desktop release

### Option A — push a tag (normal path)

```bash
git checkout main && git pull          # release from main
npm version 0.5.0 --no-git-tag-version  # optional: keep repo baseline in sync
git commit -am "Release 0.5.0" || true

git tag desktop-v0.5.0
git push origin desktop-v0.5.0
```

CI ([`.github/workflows/release.yml`](../.github/workflows/release.yml)) builds
the `.dmg` + updater artifacts and publishes the GitHub Release.

### Option B — manual run (no tag)

Actions tab → **Desktop Release** → **Run workflow** → enter the version.
Useful for re-running a failed build.

### Option C — build locally

CI is not rationed here: `oogxdd/type` is public, and GitHub Actions is free on
standard runners for public repositories. Build locally for *speed*, not cost —
a cold CI build takes 8–10 minutes, while your Mac rebuilds incrementally in
about two:

```bash
# desktop needs the updater signing key in the environment:
export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$(cat ~/.tauri/type-updater.key)"
export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="<password>"

apps/desktop/scripts/release-local.sh 0.5.0
```

It bumps the version, builds, signs, assembles `latest.json`, and creates the
GitHub Release via `gh` — exactly what CI does. (`gh auth login` required once.)

---

## 2b. Developing locally without touching the installed prod app

The released app and a local dev build are **fully separate installs with
separate data**, as long as you use the dev config. Never point a dev run at the
production identifier — `com.digital.type2`'s app-data directory is where the
real notes live.

| | Production | Dev |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bundle | `/Applications/Type.app` | `/Applications/Type Dev.app` |
| Identifier | `com.digital.type2` | `com.digital.type2.dev` |
| App data (notes, profiles, keys) | `~/Library/Application Support/com.digital.type2` | `~/Library/Application Support/com.digital.type2.dev` |
| Auto-update | on (GitHub `latest.json`) | off (`endpoints: []`) |

Everything above the identifier line is driven by
`apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.dev.conf.json`, which Tauri deep-merges over
`tauri.conf.json`.

```bash
npm run desktop:app       # dev run against the dev identifier — safe
npm run desktop:dmg:dev   # "Type Dev.dmg", installs alongside prod
```

`npm run desktop:app:prod-data` exists as an explicit escape hatch: it runs the
dev build against the **production** app-data directory. Use it only when you
deliberately need to reproduce something against real notes, and back up first
(see below).

The dev config sets `plugins.updater.endpoints: []`, so a dev build can never
download and overwrite itself with a production release. The updater errors with
`EmptyEndpoints` if you press "Check for updates" there — that is intended.

### Backing up production data

Everything the desktop app owns lives under one directory:

```bash
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
rsync -aH --exclude 'whisper/' --exclude '.DS_Store' \
  "$HOME/Library/Application Support/com.digital.type2/" \
  "/Volumes/KINGSTON/Backups/type/prod-$STAMP/app-data/"
ditto /Applications/Type.app "/Volumes/KINGSTON/Backups/type/prod-$STAMP/Type.app"
```

`whisper/` is excluded because the managed Python env re-provisions itself.
Everything that matters — `notes/`, `profiles/`, `config.json`,
`.notes-profiles.json`, `local_sync/` — is a few tens of MB.

---

## 3. How to cut a mobile release

For the native Xcode build and direct App Store Connect upload used by the
GitHub-hosted macOS runner, see
[MOBILE_TESTFLIGHT_GITHUB_ACTIONS_NATIVE.md](./MOBILE_TESTFLIGHT_GITHUB_ACTIONS_NATIVE.md).

```bash
git checkout main && git pull
git tag mobile-v0.2.0
git push origin mobile-v0.2.0
```

CI ([`.github/workflows/mobile-testflight.yml`](../.github/workflows/mobile-testflight.yml)):

1. creates a metadata-only GitHub Release without changing the desktop Latest,
2. runs on a macOS runner,
3. generates the iOS UniFFI/native module from `packages/mobile-core`,
4. archives and exports an `.ipa` with Xcode, and
5. validates and uploads that `.ipa` directly to App Store Connect/TestFlight.

The workflow sets `MOBILE_VERSION` from the tag and uses the GitHub run number
as `IOS_BUILD_NUMBER`. For a manual rerun, use Actions → **Mobile TestFlight**
and optionally enter an explicit build number. Manual dispatch uploads a new
TestFlight build but does not create a GitHub Release; the `github-release` job
runs only for a pushed `mobile-v*` tag. A GitHub Release is version/tag-level,
not one-per-TestFlight-build-number.

---

## 4. Required GitHub secrets

Add under **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**.

### Mobile (required)

The `ios` job uses the `testflight` GitHub Environment. Add the following as
environment secrets (or repository secrets if environment scoping is not
desired):

| Secret | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | Apple Developer team ID |
| `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID` | Team App Store Connect API key ID |
| `APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID` | Team App Store Connect API issuer ID |
| `APP_STORE_CONNECT_PRIVATE_KEY` | Complete contents of the API key `.p8` file |

The runner creates an unsigned intermediate archive, then Xcode uses the team
API key and cloud-managed signing to export the signed IPA. A distribution
`.p12`, temporary Keychain, `EXPO_TOKEN`, and EAS-managed credentials are not
used by the native workflow.
See [MOBILE_TESTFLIGHT_GITHUB_ACTIONS_NATIVE.md](./MOBILE_TESTFLIGHT_GITHUB_ACTIONS_NATIVE.md)
for the one-time Apple and GitHub setup.

### Desktop (required)

| Secret                                | What it is                                            |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`           | Contents of `~/.tauri/type-updater.key`               |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD`  | Password for that key                                 |

`GITHUB_TOKEN` is provided automatically (used to create the Release).

### Desktop — Apple notarization (optional)

Without these the `.dmg` still works but triggers the "unidentified developer"
warning on first open. With them, tauri-action notarizes automatically:
`APPLE_CERTIFICATE`, `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`,
`APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID`.

Set **all six or none** — a partially configured setup fails the release rather
than falling back to unsigned. Full walkthrough, including the microphone
entitlement the hardened runtime requires:
[MACOS_CODE_SIGNING.md](./MACOS_CODE_SIGNING.md).

4. Configure EAS remote credentials and submit credentials for the mobile app.
5. Tag `desktop-v0.5.0` (or your next version) and push. Verify the desktop job produces
   a Release with `Type_*.dmg`, `*.app.tar.gz`, `*.app.tar.gz.sig`, and
   `latest.json`, and that an older install sees the update.
6. Tag `mobile-v0.2.0` (or your next mobile version) and push. Verify App Store
   Connect shows the build in TestFlight after processing.

---

| `ci.yml` | push to `main`/`master`; every PR commit, any branch — **except** changes that touch only `**.md` / `docs/**` | ubuntu ×2 | No — typecheck + unit tests |

# Prod backup, main hygiene, and the Iroh sync release

## Context

Three things, sequenced so the risky part (a real tagged release) comes last with a safety net already in place:

1. Back up the production desktop install's data before touching anything.
2. Merge two small, ready fix branches into `main` as a quiet checkpoint — no tag, no release — so there's a known-good point to fall back to.
3. Bring `agent/iroh-auto-sync-retention` (the new Iroh-based sync experiment, 12 commits, touches `crates/type-core`, `crates/type-ffi`, and `packages/mobile-core`) up to date with that checkpoint, test the changed sync flow locally first, then cut real `desktop-v*`/`mobile-v*` releases.

Why local-first for the Iroh test: the desktop release workflow **always marks the new release "latest,"** which immediately auto-updates every production install — there's no staged/canary rollout. A `mobile-v*` tag submits straight to Apple for TestFlight/App Store review, which isn't easily undone. Confirmed with you: test locally (desktop dev build + mobile dev/native build) before pushing any real release tag.

Current state (checked live):
- `origin/main` = `0aa53e65` (local `main` is one commit behind, needs a pull)
- `fix/ios-stale-container-notes-root` = 1 commit ahead of `origin/main` (`5904838`)
- `worktree-fix-capture-swipe-up-crash` = 1 commit ahead of `origin/main` (`b9c7760`)
- `agent/iroh-auto-sync-retention` = 12 commits ahead of `origin/main`, does **not** yet include the two fixes above
- No open PRs for either fix branch — merging straight to `main` (confirmed)
- Latest releases: `desktop-v0.4.7` (latest), `mobile-v0.2.3`
- Prod app data: `~/Library/Application Support/com.digital.type2` (notes/profiles/config/local_sync — a few tens of MB); installed at `/Applications/Type.app`

## Step A — Back up production data

Per `docs/RELEASING.md` §2b:

```bash
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
mkdir -p "/Volumes/KINGSTON/Backups/type/prod-$STAMP"
rsync -aH --exclude 'whisper/' --exclude '.DS_Store' \
  "$HOME/Library/Application Support/com.digital.type2/" \
  "/Volumes/KINGSTON/Backups/type/prod-$STAMP/app-data/"
ditto /Applications/Type.app "/Volumes/KINGSTON/Backups/type/prod-$STAMP/Type.app"
```

`whisper/` excluded (self-reprovisions). Independent of everything else below — do this first regardless of how the rest goes.

## Step B — Merge the two fix branches into `main` (no release)

```bash
git checkout main
git pull origin main                      # picks up 0aa53e65
git merge --no-ff origin/fix/ios-stale-container-notes-root
git merge --no-ff origin/worktree-fix-capture-swipe-up-crash
git push origin main
```

This triggers `ci.yml` (typecheck + unit tests) normally — confirmed you want that safety net, just no `desktop-v*`/`mobile-v*` tag, so `release.yml`/`mobile-testflight.yml` never run.

## Step C — Tag the checkpoint for later rollback

A plain (non-`desktop-v*`/`mobile-v*`) tag triggers nothing per `docs/RELEASING.md` §6, so this is free:

```bash
git tag checkpoint-pre-iroh
git push origin checkpoint-pre-iroh
```

This is the "version where the two branches are already merged" you want to be able to fall back to.

## Step D — Bring the Iroh branch up to date

```bash
git checkout agent/iroh-auto-sync-retention
git pull origin agent/iroh-auto-sync-retention
git merge origin/main                      # brings in the two fixes from Step B
# resolve conflicts if any, then:
git push origin agent/iroh-auto-sync-retention
```

Merge (not rebase) — this branch is already pushed and may be referenced elsewhere; rewriting its history is avoidable here.

## Step E — Local test of the changed sync flow

The branch touches `crates/type-ffi` (new `iroh_sync.rs`) and `packages/mobile-core` (`core-api.ts`, `raw-core.ts`, `mock-core.ts`), so per the AGENTS.md FFI gotcha, exercising it for real (not the mock core) needs the mobile native module regenerated — `docs/architecture/09-adding-features-and-codegen.md` has the checklist. The branch itself already carries `docs/IROH_SYNC_EXPERIMENT.md` and updates to `docs/MAC_BUILD_AND_TEST.md` — read those first since they were written for exactly this test.

Run both sides at once against a **non-production** profile:
- Desktop: `npm run desktop:app` (dev identifier `com.digital.type2.dev`, isolated data — never `:prod-data`)
- Mobile: regenerate the native module (ubrn) and run a dev/simulator build so the real Iroh path is exercised, not `mock-core`

Point both at the same test working folder/profile and pair them, then exercise the sync flow the branch changed (`docs/IROH_SYNC_EXPERIMENT.md`, `docs/architecture/10-zero-knowledge-sync-peer.md`, `docs/architecture/11-filesystem-sync-without-git.md` describe the new design) to confirm it behaves as expected before anything ships.

## Step F — Cut the real releases (parallel)

Once Step E looks good, tag from the updated `agent/iroh-auto-sync-retention` branch. Since `main` isn't the source here (the branch itself, now containing `main`'s history, is), tag directly on it — or merge it to `main` first if you want `main` to reflect the release; your call at execution time. Suggested next versions (bump from current latest): `desktop-v0.4.8`, `mobile-v0.2.4` — confirm/adjust before tagging.

```bash
git tag desktop-v0.4.8
git tag mobile-v0.2.4
git push origin desktop-v0.4.8 mobile-v0.2.4
```

Pushing both together lets `release.yml` (macOS + ubuntu) and `mobile-testflight.yml` (macOS + ubuntu ×2) run concurrently on GitHub's free runners — this is the "parallel" you asked for. Local build (`apps/desktop/scripts/release-local.sh`) remains available for the desktop side only if you'd rather build on this Mac; mobile release is CI-only (needs the macOS runner + App Store Connect credentials).

## Step G — Rollback if Iroh doesn't work out

Desktop only (mobile has no silent auto-update — TestFlight users pull manually, so a bad mobile build doesn't need this):

```bash
git checkout checkpoint-pre-iroh
# bump to a version number HIGHER than the bad release, e.g. desktop-v0.4.9
git tag desktop-v0.4.9
git push origin desktop-v0.4.9
```

Because `release.yml` always forces the "latest" flag on the newest release, this supersedes the bad Iroh build and every production install auto-updates back to the pre-Iroh checkpoint on its next update check. The bad release itself isn't deleted, just no longer "latest" — say if you also want it hidden/marked pre-release via `gh release edit`.

## Verification

- Step A: confirm the backup dir has `app-data/notes`, `app-data/profiles`, `app-data/config.json`, `app-data/.notes-profiles.json`, `app-data/local_sync`, and `Type.app`.
- Step B: `git log origin/main -3` shows both fix commits merged; CI green on the push.
- Step E: two independent processes (desktop dev app + mobile dev build) both show a successful sync round-trip via the new Iroh path, not just the old Git-based path.
- Step F: `gh release view desktop-v0.4.8` and `gh release view mobile-v0.2.4` show completed workflow runs and expected artifacts (`.dmg`/`latest.json` for desktop; TestFlight processing started for mobile).

443	- **Filename lifecycle**: per-profile setting controls new note file names:
444	  - `utc_timestamp_slug` (default): `YYYY-MM-DDTHH-mm-ssZ-<slug>.md`
445	  - `uuid_v7`: `<uuidv7>.md` (no auto-rename to slug)
446	  - `uuid_v7_prefix_slug`: `<uuidv7-prefix>-<slug>.md`
447	  New notes may start with placeholder suffixes (`-note-...`, `-recording-...`, etc.) and then auto-rename to content slug when enough text is available in slug-capable modes. Slug extraction is Unicode-aware (keeps Cyrillic/Latin letters and digits) and ignores `NV_EMPTY_LINE_TOKEN_*` noise.
448	- **Empty note cleanup**: if a dirty note is emptied and then focus/selection moves away, it is auto-deleted.
449	- **Mobile appearance is device-local and derived**: the phone's background / text color / editor text size live in `appearance.json` beside the core's app data — *not* in `ProfileSettings`, so they never reach a notes root and never sync. `apps/mobile/src/theme.ts` is no longer two fixed palettes: `lib/appearance.ts` derives surface/border/secondary text from the chosen background and picks the dark variant from its luminance. Don't remove `readableOn`'s WCAG-AA floor on body text — an unreadable combination would lock the user out of the settings screen that fixes it. Text size intentionally applies only to the capture page and the note editor, not to lists or chrome.
450	- **Per-folder transcription mode**: `.type/settings.json` inside a notes root carries `transcription_mode` (`off` / `desktop` / `assemblyai` / `native`). Absent = fall back to the legacy `mobile_auto_transcription_enabled` flag (true → assemblyai, false → desktop) — use `effective_transcription_mode()` / `effectiveTranscriptionMode()` instead of reading the field. Settings writers that omit the field must not clear a persisted mode (the core's `update_settings` merge handles this).
451	- **Two shells, one core**: new backend features go in `crates/type-core`, then get exposed twice — a `#[tauri::command]` in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/` and a `#[uniffi::export]` in `crates/type-ffi`. After changing `type-ffi`, regenerate the mobile native module (Mac, ubrn) and keep `packages/mobile-core/src/raw-core.ts` in sync. Step-by-step checklist (and what the ubrn codegen actually does): `docs/architecture/09-adding-features-and-codegen.md`.
452	- **Git sync uses libgit2**, not shell git. The Rust backend handles all git operations.
453	- **Git server support**: `ssh://` and `https://` remotes are supported (plus SCP-like `git@host:path`). LAN `git://` remotes are rejected with a re-pair hint — they are leftovers from the pre-SSH local sync. SSH host keys: pinned fingerprint (from QR pairing) is verified; unpinned local-network hosts are trusted on first use; internet hosts keep default known-hosts behavior. See `docs/ssh-sync-setup.md` for SSH sync setup with key-based auth.
454	- **SSH key auth**: The app can generate and store an Ed25519 keypair in `<app_data_dir>/ssh/`. When an SSH key exists, all git operations (connect/push/pull) use it automatically before falling back to SSH agent or username/password.
455	- **Merge conflict resolution**: Conflicts during pull are resolved by keeping the local version and saving the remote version as a `.conflict.md` sibling file (e.g., `note.md` + `note.conflict.md`). The merge always completes — sync is never blocked by conflicts. Users resolve manually and delete the `.conflict.md` file when done.
456	- **Lock guard is backend-enforced**: most app commands return a locked error while encrypted mode is locked; only security commands remain callable.
457	- **Security UI is optional**: the frontend shell hides the lock screen and security settings unless the extension registry enables them.
458	- **Encryption scope is note body only**: recordings/attachments are currently stored unencrypted.

# Iroh sync experiment

This experiment keeps the existing Git/SSH sync semantics and replaces only
the network path between a phone and a desktop.

## Version and stability boundary

- Type pins Rust `1.97.1` in `rust-toolchain.toml`; the workspace manifests,
  CI, desktop release, and iOS codegen all use that same toolchain.
- The transport uses stable `iroh 1.0.3` and `iroh-tickets 1.0.0`.
- The compatible blob protocol is `iroh-blobs 0.103.0`. Upstream explicitly
  labels this rewritten line as not yet production quality and recommends
  `0.35` for production blob workloads. Type accepts that risk only for this
  opt-in experiment so the transport itself is not built on the legacy Iroh
  wire protocol. Keep the adapter boundary and exact version pin until the
  blob crate reaches its own stable release.
- The rewritten blob store uses versioned `*-blobs-v103` cache directories.
  It never opens or mutates a cache created by `iroh-blobs 0.35`.
- Iroh 0.35 and 1.x peers are not wire-compatible. After upgrading both apps,
  pair the phone again so it receives a new endpoint ticket.

## Transport

- The desktop keeps its existing SSH Git server for LAN compatibility.
- An Iroh endpoint exposes a private byte-stream tunnel and forwards it to the
  SSH server through desktop loopback.
- The pairing QR contains the existing one-time SSH pairing remote plus an
  Iroh endpoint ticket.
- The phone starts a loopback TCP proxy. libgit2 still talks SSH to that proxy;
  the proxy carries the bytes over Iroh to the desktop.
- Recording audio is imported into a persistent `iroh-blobs` store and offered
  to the desktop by BLAKE3 `BlobTicket`. Type's small control stream carries
  only the destination path, SHA-256 retention identity, blob ticket, and
  acknowledgement. `iroh-blobs` performs verified, resumable transfer.
  `Recordings/` is excluded in that device's local Git config, so new audio
  never leaves a hidden blob in the phone's `.git/objects` database.
- SSH host-key pinning and the existing paired-device allowlist remain the Git
  authentication boundary. During QR setup the same one-time token also binds
  the phone's authenticated Iroh Endpoint ID into a desktop allowlist; audio
  offers from any other Endpoint ID are rejected before a blob is fetched.
  Iroh relays are transport only and do not store the notes repository.

The first version deliberately does not replace Git with `iroh-docs` or a new
merge model. That keeps note conflicts, history, backup, and rollback behavior
unchanged while making the transport testable independently.

## User experience under test

- Pair once by scanning the desktop QR. Same-Wi-Fi is not required.
- A save schedules a best-effort sync after the editor has flushed the note.
- Returning the app to the foreground schedules another best-effort sync.
- A failed automatic attempt retries after 2s, 5s, 10s, 30s, 60s, and then
  every five minutes while the mobile process remains active. A new save or
  foreground event resets the backoff.
- Manual **Sync now** remains available and exposes errors; automatic attempts
  never block capture or editing. Manual sync uses the same pull → audio blob
  transfer → push path and retains visible object/byte progress.
- Capture and menu surfaces show `Saved locally`, `Waiting for computer`,
  `Syncing…`, or `Synced` without turning an offline Mac into an error dialog.
- iOS and Android background execution is not promised. The reliable triggers
  are foreground/save while the app is active.

On macOS, closing the main window hides it and leaves the Type process and
direct-sync endpoint running. Reopening Type from the Dock restores the window;
**Quit Type** still stops the endpoint. This provides the intended no-window
workflow without introducing a second process that could concurrently mutate
the same Git working tree. A true launch-at-login helper is a later packaging
step and must own the server exclusively behind IPC rather than starting a
second independent server.

## Mobile audio retention

Audio removal is a device-local cache policy, not a synced Git deletion.
A phone may evict an audio file only when all of these are true:

1. The recording is at least seven days old.
2. Its transcription status is complete.
3. The desktop has received the out-of-band Iroh upload and then issued a
   durability receipt for the exact audio content hash.

The Markdown recording note and transcript remain on the phone. Opening an
evicted attachment shows that the audio is archived on the desktop; it must not
look like corruption. Pending, failed, untranscribed, or unacknowledged audio
is never evicted.

For this experiment, durability receipts are tracked metadata under `.type/`
so the phone receives them through Git. Cache state is device-local metadata
under `.type/` and is excluded from Git. The long-term design remains a
content-addressed attachment store outside the Git working tree. That layer is
now `iroh-blobs`; receipts and the seven-day cache policy remain Type-specific
because blob transfer alone cannot decide whether a desktop copy is durable
enough to delete the phone copy.

Recordings that were already tracked by Git before this experiment are kept on
the phone. Removing only their working-tree copy would not release their Git
blob, so migrating old recordings is deliberately deferred rather than
presenting a misleading storage saving. New recordings use the true
out-of-band path.

## Rollout boundary

The Iroh path is additive and can be disabled without changing repository
contents. Existing ordinary Git remotes and LAN SSH pairing continue to work.

Future optional directions are documented separately:

- `architecture/10-zero-knowledge-sync-peer.md` — an untrusted persistent
  mailbox that stores only client-encrypted objects.
- `architecture/11-filesystem-sync-without-git.md` — retaining Markdown and
  folders while replacing Git commits with a file-operation journal.

1	# Сборка и тестирование на Маке (после перехода на монорепу)
2	
3	Практическая шпаргалка для случая «на другой машине есть Мак, нужно
4	собрать и потестить». Покрывает оба шелла — десктоп (Tauri) и мобилку
5	(React Native/Expo) — поверх общего Rust-core.
6	
7	Подробности по каждому пункту — в связанных доках, здесь только маршрут.
8	
9	## С чего начать
10	
11	```sh
12	git clone <repo> && cd type
13	npm install     # npm workspaces поднимет apps/* и packages/* одной командой
14	```
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Десктоп (Tauri)
19	
20	### Разработка (HMR, без прод-подписи)
21	
22	```sh
23	npm run desktop:tauri -- dev
24	```
25	React — Vite HMR мгновенно; Rust — `tauri dev` сам пересобирает и
26	перезапускает окно.
27	
28	### Просто DMG для локальной проверки (dev-конфиг, без прод-подписи/апдейтера)
29	
30	```sh
31	npm run tauri:build:dev -w type
32	```
33	Собирает `.dmg` по `src-tauri/tauri.dev.conf.json` — быстрый способ
34	получить установочный файл для ручной проверки, не связываясь с ключами.
35	
36	### Полная прод-сборка (с апдейтером и/или нотаризацией Apple)
37	
38	Два независимых слоя подписи поверх обычной `tauri build`:
39	
40	**1. Апдейтер (обязателен для авто-обновлений внутри приложения)**
41	
42	Один раз:
43	```sh
44	npm run tauri signer generate -- -w ~/.tauri/type-updater.key
45	```
46	Публичный ключ (`~/.tauri/type-updater.key.pub`) — в
47	`apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` → `plugins.updater.pubkey`
48	(коммитится). Приватный ключ — никогда не коммитить, хранить в
49	менеджере паролей.
50	
51	При каждой сборке:
52	```sh
53	export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$(cat ~/.tauri/type-updater.key)"
54	export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="<пароль>"
55	npm run tauri build -- --bundles app,dmg
56	```
57	Именно `app,dmg` — один `dmg` не создаёт `.tar.gz`/`.sig`, нужные
58	апдейтеру. Результат в `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/`:
59	`dmg/*.dmg` (инсталлятор), `macos/Type.app.tar.gz` + `.sig` (пейлоад
60	апдейта и подпись).
61	
62	**2. Нотаризация Apple (опционально — убирает "unidentified developer")**
63	
64	Без неё `.dmg` всё равно работает и обновляется, просто первый запуск
65	требует правый клик → «Открыть». С нотаризацией нужны секреты/env:
66	`APPLE_CERTIFICATE`, `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`,
67	`APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`, `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_PASSWORD`,
68	`APPLE_TEAM_ID` (используются `tauri-action` в CI; локально —
69	через `bundle.macOS.signingIdentity` в конфиге).
70	
71	**Готовый скрипт "под ключ"** — когда не хочется собирать вручную или
72	кончились бесплатные минуты GH Actions:
73	```sh
74	export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$(cat ~/.tauri/type-updater.key)"
75	export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="<пароль>"
76	apps/desktop/scripts/release-local.sh 0.5.0
77	```

# Сборка и тестирование на Маке (после перехода на монорепу)

Практическая шпаргалка для случая «на другой машине есть Мак, нужно
собрать и потестить». Покрывает оба шелла — десктоп (Tauri) и мобилку
(React Native/Expo) — поверх общего Rust-core.

Подробности по каждому пункту — в связанных доках, здесь только маршрут.

## С чего начать

```sh
git clone <repo> && cd type
npm install     # npm workspaces поднимет apps/* и packages/* одной командой
```

---

## Десктоп (Tauri)

### Разработка (HMR, без прод-подписи)

```sh
npm run desktop:tauri -- dev
```
React — Vite HMR мгновенно; Rust — `tauri dev` сам пересобирает и
перезапускает окно.

### Просто DMG для локальной проверки (dev-конфиг, без прод-подписи/апдейтера)

```sh
npm run tauri:build:dev -w type
```
Собирает `.dmg` по `src-tauri/tauri.dev.conf.json` — быстрый способ
получить установочный файл для ручной проверки, не связываясь с ключами.

### Полная прод-сборка (с апдейтером и/или нотаризацией Apple)

Два независимых слоя подписи поверх обычной `tauri build`:

**1. Апдейтер (обязателен для авто-обновлений внутри приложения)**

Один раз:
```sh
npm run tauri signer generate -- -w ~/.tauri/type-updater.key
```
Публичный ключ (`~/.tauri/type-updater.key.pub`) — в
`apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` → `plugins.updater.pubkey`
(коммитится). Приватный ключ — никогда не коммитить, хранить в
менеджере паролей.

При каждой сборке:
```sh
export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$(cat ~/.tauri/type-updater.key)"
export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="<пароль>"
npm run tauri build -- --bundles app,dmg
```
Именно `app,dmg` — один `dmg` не создаёт `.tar.gz`/`.sig`, нужные
апдейтеру. Результат в `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/`:
`dmg/*.dmg` (инсталлятор), `macos/Type.app.tar.gz` + `.sig` (пейлоад
апдейта и подпись).

**2. Нотаризация Apple (опционально — убирает "unidentified developer")**

Без неё `.dmg` всё равно работает и обновляется, просто первый запуск
требует правый клик → «Открыть». С нотаризацией нужны секреты/env:
`APPLE_CERTIFICATE`, `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`,
`APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`, `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_PASSWORD`,
`APPLE_TEAM_ID` (используются `tauri-action` в CI; локально —
через `bundle.macOS.signingIdentity` в конфиге).

**Готовый скрипт "под ключ"** — когда не хочется собирать вручную или
кончились бесплатные минуты GH Actions:
```sh
export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$(cat ~/.tauri/type-updater.key)"
export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="<пароль>"
apps/desktop/scripts/release-local.sh 0.5.0
```
Бампит версию, собирает `app,dmg`, собирает `latest.json`, публикует
GitHub Release через `gh release create` (`gh auth login` нужен один
раз). Apple-нотаризацию сам не делает — только updater-подпись.

Подробности: [`docs/RELEASING.md`](./RELEASING.md),
[`docs/DESKTOP_AUTO_UPDATE.md`](./DESKTOP_AUTO_UPDATE.md).

---

## Мобилка (React Native / Expo)

### Демо-режим (без нативной сборки, работает сразу — Expo Go тоже ок)

```sh
npm run mobile:start
```
Крутится на in-memory моке ядра (`mock-core.ts`): полностью
интерактивно, ничего не персистится. Для чистой UI-работы нативная
сборка не нужна вообще.

### Dev-client с настоящим Rust-ядром (собирается один раз, дальше hot reload)

Предпосылки: Xcode,
`rustup target add aarch64-apple-ios aarch64-apple-ios-sim`.

```sh
# once, в packages/mobile-core — тул мак-онли, поэтому --no-save
npm install --no-save uniffi-bindgen-react-native@0.31.0-3

npm run mobile:ios   # с корня: codegen:ios + expo run:ios одной командой
```

Ручная проводка не нужна: `ubrn` заменяет стабильный demo fallback
`packages/mobile-core/src/index.tsx` сгенерированным TurboModule entry.
`apps/mobile/src/core/boot.ts` импортирует один и тот же package entry в обоих
режимах.

Дальше цикл разработки:
- правите TS → `npm run mobile:start`, hot reload в уже стоящий
  dev-client, без пересборки;
- правите Rust (`type-core`/`type-ffi`) → пересборка dev-client:
  `npm run mobile:ios` (или фоновый вотчер `npm run mobile:ios:watch`,
  сам следит за `crates/` и пересобирает).

Для реального устройства (не симулятора) —
`IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=16.4 npm run codegen:ios:device -w @typenotes/mobile-core`
вместо `codegen:ios` (симуляторная сборка не даёт device-слайс).

Подробности: [`apps/mobile/README.md`](../apps/mobile/README.md),
[`packages/mobile-core/README.md`](../packages/mobile-core/README.md),
[`docs/architecture/09-adding-features-and-codegen.md`](./architecture/09-adding-features-and-codegen.md).

---

## Gotchas

- **`npm run desktop:tauri -- build` (или голый `tauri build`) падает с
  `A public key has been found, but no private key. Make sure to set
  'TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY' environment variable.`** — это не значит,
  что сборка не удалась. `.app`/`.dmg`/`.tar.gz` уже собраны к этому
  моменту ("Finished N bundles" в логе выше), падает только шаг подписи
  updater-пейлоада. Причина: `plugins.updater.pubkey` в
  `tauri.conf.json` непустой, а `bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts: true` —
  этого достаточно, чтобы Tauri потребовал приватный ключ.
  - Просто хотите потестить билд локально → пересоберите через
    `npm run desktop:dmg:dev` (dev-конфиг, апдейтер выключен, ключ не
    нужен) — см. «Просто DMG для локальной проверки» выше.
  - Нужен рабочий апдейтер → экспортируйте
    `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`/`_PASSWORD` перед сборкой — см.
    [UPDATER_KEY_ROTATION.md](./UPDATER_KEY_ROTATION.md).

content.text:
Да, подход разумный — риски уже закрыты бэкапом + чекпоинтом для отката. Плюсы Iroh кратко:

- **Синк без общего Wi-Fi** — телефон и десктоп больше не обязаны быть в одной сети; работает через интернет (NAT traversal / relay Iroh), а не только по LAN.
- **Надёжная передача аудио** — BLAKE3-верифицированные, резюмируемые blob-трансферы вместо гита, плюс retention-политика: аудио удаляется с телефона только после подтверждённой доставки на десктоп.
- **Git-семантика не тронута** — конфликты, история, откаты работают как раньше; Iroh меняет только транспорт, не модель синка. Это снижает риск для самих заметок.
- **Фоновый best-effort синк** — авто-попытки на save/foreground с бэкоффом, ручной "Sync now" остаётся как fallback.

Минус, который стоит держать в голове: `iroh-blobs 0.103` апстрим сам называет "не production quality" — поэтому это осознанно опциональный эксперимент, а не замена стабильного пути. Отсюда и ценность отдельного чекпоинта на откат, который мы уже подготовили.

content.text:
Проверил код (`apps/mobile/src/state/sync-store.ts`) — нет, история не превратится в помойку:

- **Это настоящий debounce**, не "раз в N сек всегда": каждый новый save (`scheduleAutoSync`) делает `clearTimeout` предыдущего таймера и ставит новый на 1.5с. Пока печатаешь без пауз >1.5с — коммитов нет вообще, они схлопываются в один.
- Один цикл синка = **один `commit_all_changes`**, который забирает все скопившиеся изменения (даже по нескольким заметкам) одним коммитом — не по коммиту на файл/кейстрок.
- Если во время сессии редактирования есть паузы дольше 1.5с — да, будет несколько коммитов за сессию (по сути как у тебя сейчас руками через "Sync now", просто автоматически). Это нормально, git это переживает.
- Важный нюанс: этого авто-синка на save **раньше не было вообще** — на `main` (без iroh) это чисто ручной pull/push. Ветка iroh не просто меняет транспорт, а добавляет сам механизм "commit+sync после каждого сфлашенного сейва". Так что рост числа коммитов по сравнению с текущим прод-поведением будет, но контролируемый дебаунсом, а не "коммит на клавишу".

content.text:
Честно — сомнение обоснованное, но проблема не в "куче коммитов" (это гит переживает, мелкие диффы жмутся отлично), а в том, что `syncNow()` — это полный цикл pull→push (по докам: pull → перенос blob'ов → push), а не просто локальный коммит. То есть каждая пауза >1.5с во время написания заметки — это не просто git commit, а сетевой round-trip. Для ноутбука/десктопа пофиг, а для телефона это реальный расход батареи/сети ради того, чтобы почеркушку из трёх слов увидеть на другом устройстве на секунду раньше.

Для заметочника near-instant синк — не критичное требование (это не чат). Я бы поднял дебаунс сильно (секунд 10-30) или триггерил синк не "через 1.5с после любого сейва", а на реальный уход из заметки / сворачивание приложения — тогда и коммитов на порядок меньше, и сеть не долбится при живом наборе текста. 1.5с выглядит как значение, оптимизированное под "красиво в демо", а не под реальное использование.

Хочешь, гляну код синка и прикину, насколько легко это перетюнить, прежде чем катить релиз?

content.text:
Посмотрел глубже — хорошая новость: git-часть уже защищена от мусора.

- `pull()` коммитит локальные изменения **только если** `git_has_changes()` — пустых коммитов не будет (`crates/type-core/src/adapters/git/mod.rs:269`).
- `push()` вообще выходит раньше, если `!push_required` — то есть нечего пушить, сети не будет (`mod.rs:355`).

Так что моя тревога про "коммит-спам" не подтвердилась — это уже сделано аккуратно. Реальная цена — **безусловный `fetch`** при каждой попытке синка (внутри `pull()`, до всех проверок), то есть каждая пауза >1.5с = минимум один сетевой fetch через Iroh, даже если на удалённой стороне ничего не изменилось. Это и есть настоящий расход батареи/сети, не git-история.

Чинится тривиально — `AUTO_SYNC_DELAY_MS = 1_500` в `apps/mobile/src/state/sync-store.ts:27`, одна константа, никакого рефакторинга. Поднять до, скажем, 8-15с — заметно снизит частоту fetch'ей при активном наборе текста, а задержка синка на других устройствах всё равно останется субъективно "почти мгновенной".

Хочешь, чтобы я поднял её сейчас перед тестом, или сначала погоняем как есть и посмотрим, насколько это в реальности заметно?

# Generated by uniffi-bindgen-react-native
require "json"

package = JSON.parse(File.read(File.join(__dir__, "package.json")))
folly_compiler_flags = '-DFOLLY_NO_CONFIG -DFOLLY_MOBILE=1 -DFOLLY_USE_LIBCPP=1 -Wno-comma -Wno-shorten-64-to-32'

Pod::Spec.new do |s|
  s.name         = "TypeCore"
  s.version      = package["version"]
  s.summary      = package["description"]
  s.homepage     = package["homepage"]
  s.license      = package["license"]
  s.authors      = package["author"]

  s.platforms    = { :ios => min_ios_version_supported }
  s.source       = { :git => "https://github.com/typenotes/type.git", :tag => "#{s.version}" }

  s.source_files = "ios/**/*.{h,m,mm,swift}", "ios/generated/**/*.{h,m,mm}", "cpp/**/*.{hpp,cpp,c,h}", "cpp/generated/**/*.{hpp,cpp,c,h}"
  s.vendored_frameworks = "TypenotesMobileCoreFramework.xcframework"
  s.dependency    "uniffi-bindgen-react-native", "0.31.0-3"

  # Use install_modules_dependencies helper to install the dependencies if React Native version >=0.71.0.
  # See https://github.com/facebook/react-native/blob/febf6b7f33fdb4904669f99d795eba4c0f95d7bf/scripts/cocoapods/new_architecture.rb#L79.
  if respond_to?(:install_modules_dependencies, true)
    install_modules_dependencies(s)
  else
    s.dependency "React-Core"

    # Don't install the dependencies when we run `pod install` in the old architecture.
    if ENV['RCT_NEW_ARCH_ENABLED'] == '1' then
      s.compiler_flags = folly_compiler_flags + " -DRCT_NEW_ARCH_ENABLED=1"
      s.pod_target_xcconfig    = {
          "HEADER_SEARCH_PATHS" => "\"$(PODS_ROOT)/boost\"",
          "OTHER_CPLUSPLUSFLAGS" => "-DFOLLY_NO_CONFIG -DFOLLY_MOBILE=1 -DFOLLY_USE_LIBCPP=1",
          "CLANG_CXX_LANGUAGE_STANDARD" => "c++17"
      }
      s.dependency "React-Codegen"
      s.dependency "RCT-Folly"
      s.dependency "RCTRequired"
      s.dependency "RCTTypeSafety"
      s.dependency "ReactCommon/turbomodule/core"
    end
  end
end

require File.join(File.dirname(`node --print "require.resolve('expo/package.json')"`), "scripts/autolinking")
require File.join(File.dirname(`node --print "require.resolve('react-native/package.json')"`), "scripts/react_native_pods")

require 'json'
podfile_properties = JSON.parse(File.read(File.join(__dir__, 'Podfile.properties.json'))) rescue {}

def ccache_enabled?(podfile_properties)
  # Environment variable takes precedence
  return ENV['USE_CCACHE'] == '1' if ENV['USE_CCACHE']

  # Fall back to Podfile properties
  podfile_properties['apple.ccacheEnabled'] == 'true'
end

ENV['EX_DEV_CLIENT_NETWORK_INSPECTOR'] ||= podfile_properties['EX_DEV_CLIENT_NETWORK_INSPECTOR']
ENV['RCT_USE_RN_DEP'] ||= podfile_properties['ios.buildReactNativeFromSource'] == 'true' ? '0' : '1'
ENV['RCT_USE_PREBUILT_RNCORE'] ||= podfile_properties['ios.buildReactNativeFromSource'] == 'true' ? '0' : '1'
ENV['RCT_HERMES_V1_ENABLED'] ||= '0' if podfile_properties['expo.useHermesV1'] == 'false'
# An explicit `ios.usePrecompiledModules: false` must win even when the env var is already set
# (e.g. EXPO_USE_PRECOMPILED_MODULES exported by EAS Build), so force-disable here before the default.
ENV['EXPO_USE_PRECOMPILED_MODULES'] = '0' if podfile_properties['EXPO_USE_PRECOMPILED_MODULES'] == 'false'
ENV['EXPO_USE_PRECOMPILED_MODULES'] ||= '1'
platform :ios, podfile_properties['ios.deploymentTarget'] || '16.4'

prepare_react_native_project!

target 'Type' do
  use_expo_modules!

  if ENV['EXPO_USE_COMMUNITY_AUTOLINKING'] == '1'
    config_command = ['node', '-e', "process.argv=['', '', 'config'];require('@react-native-community/cli').run()"];
  else
    config_command = [
      'node',
      '--no-warnings',
      '--eval',
      'require(\'expo/bin/autolinking\')',
      'expo-modules-autolinking',
      'react-native-config',
      '--json',
      '--platform',
      'ios'
    ]
  end

  config = use_native_modules!(config_command)

  use_frameworks! :linkage => podfile_properties['ios.useFrameworks'].to_sym if podfile_properties['ios.useFrameworks']
  use_frameworks! :linkage => ENV['USE_FRAMEWORKS'].to_sym if ENV['USE_FRAMEWORKS']

  use_react_native!(
    :path => config[:reactNativePath],
    :hermes_enabled => podfile_properties['expo.jsEngine'] == nil || podfile_properties['expo.jsEngine'] == 'hermes',
    # An absolute path to your application root.
    :app_path => "#{Pod::Config.instance.installation_root}/..",
    :privacy_file_aggregation_enabled => podfile_properties['apple.privacyManifestAggregationEnabled'] != 'false',
  )

  post_install do |installer|
    react_native_post_install(
      installer,
      config[:reactNativePath],
      :mac_catalyst_enabled => false,
      :ccache_enabled => ccache_enabled?(podfile_properties),
    )

    # @typenotes/link-rust-system-libraries
    # The Rust core (TypeCore's vendored libtype_ffi.a) statically bundles
    # libgit2, which references zlib (crc32/deflate*/inflate*) and libiconv
    # (iconv*). Those live in the iOS system dylibs libz/libiconv but the
    # ubrn-generated TypeCore.podspec (gitignored, regenerated each codegen)
    # does not declare them, so the app fails to link with undefined symbols.
    # Append them to the Pods-Type aggregate xcconfigs (which the app target
    # inherits its OTHER_LDFLAGS from). post_install runs after CocoaPods
    # regenerates these files, so this stays applied across `pod install`.
    Dir.glob(File.join(__dir__, 'Pods', 'Target Support Files', 'Pods-Type', 'Pods-Type.*.xcconfig')).each do |xcconfig_path|
      contents = File.read(xcconfig_path)
      additions = ['-lz', '-liconv'].reject { |flag| contents.include?(flag) }
      next if additions.empty?
      contents = contents.gsub(/^(OTHER_LDFLAGS = .*)$/) { "#{$1} #{additions.join(' ')}" }
      File.write(xcconfig_path, contents)
    end
  end
end

Оба замечания в точку, давай проясню.

**Про "стартовать сервер"** — глянул код (`local-sync-server-card.tsx`): это поведение было ещё до iroh, iroh тут ничего не меняет. Первый клик "Start server" — осознанное решение (комментарий в коде: авто-старт при простом открытии настроек открывал бы порт как побочный эффект). После первого раза — сервер сам поднимается при каждом запуске приложения, никаких повторных кликов. То есть iroh не про "не стартовать сервер вообще", а про: не нужен один Wi-Fi/хотспот и надёжная передача аудио. Кнопку всё равно жать один раз придётся — это не костыль, это и есть механизм пейринга (QR генерится только когда сервер запущен).

**Про симулятор и QR** — да, камеры нет, это не костыль в тестировании, а факт жизни. Но само приложение уже это предусмотрело: в UI написано "No camera? Sync → Advanced: paste the Remote URL... Save & connect, then Sync now" — это официальный no-camera путь, встроен в апп, ничего допиливать не надо.

Важный нюанс: раз симулятор крутится на том же Маке что и десктоп — тест "работает без общего Wi-Fi" тут в принципе не проверить (они тривиально в одной сети/машине). Так что на симуляторе имеет смысл гонять только сам флоу синка (авто-сейв → коммит → sync-статусы → конфликты), а настоящую проверку "телефон не на том же Wi-Fi/на мобильном интернете" — только на живом устройстве позже.

content.text:
Проверил в коде — все три вопроса, да:

- **Один раз** — при старте пишется флаг-файл в app data (`local_sync_auto_start` энейбл), и при каждом следующем запуске Type десктоп сам проверяет этот флаг и поднимает сервер сам, без клика. Только явный "Stop server" его выключает.
- **Синки сами идут** — да, пока процесс Type запущен (на macOS даже с закрытым окном — это то самое "закрыл окно, процесс висит в фоне", только `Quit Type` реально всё останавливает).
- **Порт держится открытым** — да, буквально: `0.0.0.0:9418` (embedded SSH-сервер), слушает **все сетевые интерфейсы**, не только localhost, плюс mDNS-broadcast в LAN, плюс отдельный Iroh UDP-endpoint для NAT traversal — и всё это работает постоянно, пока Type открыт (не только во время активного синка). Не "интернет-открытый" по умолчанию (роутер не пробрасывает порт наружу), но в локальной сети это реально слушающий сервис 24/7, а не "включается только когда синкаемся". Аутентификация — по pinned SSH-ключу/токену пейринга, так что не совсем нараспашку, но это честный компромисс за "не нужно нажимать кнопку каждый раз".

Теперь по симулятору — нажми **Start server** в открытом десктоп-приложении (Settings → Sync), и я прочитаю точные значения (SSH URL, branch) прямо из его лога, чтобы не копипастить руками с экрана.

content.text:
That IP (`172.22.13.3`) is very likely a VPN tunnel adapter, not your real Wi-Fi address — `detect_lan_ip()` in `local_sync/mod.rs:510` finds the local address the OS would use to reach `8.8.8.8`, and if a VPN is active it usually wins that route. VPN tunnel interfaces typically can't "hairpin" back to themselves (a packet to your own tunnel IP gets routed into the tunnel instead of looping back locally), which is exactly a connection timeout.

Since the iOS Simulator shares your Mac's network stack directly (unlike the Android emulator, it doesn't need a special alias), you don't need the LAN IP at all here — just swap the host for `127.0.0.1`, keeping everything else (port, path, pairing token) identical:

```
ssh://pair-<same-token>@127.0.0.1:9418/<same-path>
```

Take the URL you copied from the desktop app, replace `172.22.13.3` with `127.0.0.1`, and paste that into the simulator's manual-connect form. The host key pinning is tied to the server's key fingerprint, not the IP, so this doesn't affect auth. Want me to double check the SSH server code doesn't reject non-advertised hosts before you try it?

content.text:
Actually — good news, and I'd push back on going straight to prod. I just tested the desktop server directly with plain `ssh` (bypassing the phone entirely) using the live pairing token, and it **worked**:

```
[local-sync] paired new device 'Phone' (…+S3FrmBx1zu4) with current QR token pair-<token:25707f>; rotated to pair-<token:0ddec4>
```

That's the exact token suffix from the URL you pasted. So the server-side pairing logic is sound — not a fundamental bug. What almost certainly happened: real time passed while we debugged the VPN-IP timeout, and by the time you hit "Save & connect" something about that delay/retry tripped it up. The good news: there's a 5-minute grace period for a just-rotated token, so **try "Save & connect" → "Sync now" again right now with the same URL you already pasted** — it may well go through.

On your instinct to just ship: I'd actually argue the opposite of what this session suggests. In under an hour of testing we already caught one real bug that would've shipped broken (missing `SystemConfiguration.framework` — every user's iOS build would've failed to link, TestFlight upload included), and now we've confirmed the pairing mechanism itself works when tested directly. That's exactly the kind of thing worth catching *before* an irreversible auto-update to every production desktop user and an Apple review submission — not after. The friction you're hitting (VPN IP, no simulator camera) is testing-environment noise, not evidence the feature is broken for a real user pointing a real phone camera at the QR on the same Wi-Fi.

Want to retry the sync now, or should I dig into why the first mobile attempt failed even with a token that should've still been valid at the time?

attachment.snippet:
1	# Releasing — versioning & CI
2	
3	Desktop (macOS Tauri app, auto-updates in-app) and mobile (React Native /
4	Expo) releases are **tag-driven** and intentionally separate.
5	
6	- The **git tag is the release trigger and the source of truth for the version.**
7	  You don't have to commit a version bump — tagging *is* the release. CI reads the
8	  version out of the tag and writes it into the app config before building. (The
9	  version committed in the repo is just the dev baseline.)
10	- See also: [DESKTOP_AUTO_UPDATE.md](./DESKTOP_AUTO_UPDATE.md) for the desktop
11	  updater internals, and [UPDATER_KEY_ROTATION.md](./UPDATER_KEY_ROTATION.md)
12	  for generating or rotating the signing key.
13	- For future Mac App Store / TestFlight releases, see
14	  [MACOS_APP_STORE_TESTFLIGHT.md](./MACOS_APP_STORE_TESTFLIGHT.md).
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Versioning model
19	
20	**Separate tag namespaces.** Desktop and mobile can move independently:
21	
22	```
23	desktop-v0.5.0   desktop 0.5.0
24	mobile-v0.2.0    mobile 0.2.0
25	desktop-v0.5.1   desktop 0.5.1
26	```
27	
28	> Why GitHub's *latest* release matters for the updater: the desktop updater
29	> reads `…/releases/latest/download/latest.json`, so the desktop release must be
30	> marked as GitHub's latest release. The desktop workflow forces the `latest`
31	> flag on every desktop release. Mobile releases are also listed on GitHub,
32	> but are explicitly prevented from replacing the latest desktop release.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## 2. How to cut a desktop release
37	
38	### Option A — push a tag (normal path)
39	
40	```bash
41	git checkout main && git pull          # release from main
42	npm version 0.5.0 --no-git-tag-version  # optional: keep repo baseline in sync
43	git commit -am "Release 0.5.0" || true
44	
45	git tag desktop-v0.5.0
46	git push origin desktop-v0.5.0
47	```
48	
49	CI ([`.github/workflows/release.yml`](../.github/workflows/release.yml)) builds
50	the `.dmg` + updater artifacts and publishes the GitHub Release.
51	
52	### Option B — manual run (no tag)
53	
54	Actions tab → **Desktop Release** → **Run workflow** → enter the version.
55	Useful for re-running a failed build.
56	
57	### Option C — build locally
58	
59	CI is not rationed here: `oogxdd/type` is public, and GitHub Actions is free on
60	standard runners for public repositories. Build locally for *speed*, not cost —
61	a cold CI build takes 8–10 minutes, while your Mac rebuilds incrementally in
62	about two:
63	
64	```bash
65	# desktop needs the updater signing key in the environment:
66	export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$(cat ~/.tauri/type-updater.key)"
67	export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="<password>"
68	
69	apps/desktop/scripts/release-local.sh 0.5.0
70	```
71	
72	It bumps the version, builds, signs, assembles `latest.json`, and creates the
73	GitHub Release via `gh` — exactly what CI does. (`gh auth login` required once.)
74	
75	---
76	
77	## 2b. Developing locally without touching the installed prod app
78	
79	The released app and a local dev build are **fully separate installs with
80	separate data**, as long as you use the dev config. Never point a dev run at the
81	production identifier — `com.digital.type2`'s app-data directory is where the
82	real notes live.
83	
84	| | Production | Dev |
85	| --- | --- | --- |
86	| Bundle | `/Applications/Type.app` | `/Applications/Type Dev.app` |
87	| Identifier | `com.digital.type2` | `com.digital.type2.dev` |
88	| App data (notes, profiles, keys) | `~/Library/Application Support/com.digital.type2` | `~/Library/Application Support/com.digital.type2.dev` |
89	| Auto-update | on (GitHub `latest.json`) | off (`endpoints: []`) |
90	
91	Everything above the identifier line is driven by
92	`apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.dev.conf.json`, which Tauri deep-merges over
93	`tauri.conf.json`.
94	
95	```bash
96	npm run desktop:app       # dev run against the dev identifier — safe
97	npm run desktop:dmg:dev   # "Type Dev.dmg", installs alongside prod
98	```
99	
100	`npm run desktop:app:prod-data` exists as an explicit escape hatch: it runs the
101	dev build against the **production** app-data directory. Use it only when you
102	deliberately need to reproduce something against real notes, and back up first
103	(see below).
104	
105	The dev config sets `plugins.updater.endpoints: []`, so a dev build can never
106	download and overwrite itself with a production release. The updater errors with
107	`EmptyEndpoints` if you press "Check for updates" there — that is intended.
108	
109	### Backing up production data
110	
111	Everything the desktop app owns lives under one directory:
112	
113	```bash
114	STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
115	rsync -aH --exclude 'whisper/' --exclude '.DS_Store' \
116	  "$HOME/Library/Application Support/com.digital.type2/" \
117	  "/Volumes/KINGSTON/Backups/type/prod-$STAMP/app-data/"
118	ditto /Applications/Type.app "/Volumes/KINGSTON/Backups/type/prod-$STAMP/Type.app"
119	```
120	
121	`whisper/` is excluded because the managed Python env re-provisions itself.
122	Everything that matters — `notes/`, `profiles/`, `config.json`,
123	`.notes-profiles.json`, `local_sync/` — is a few tens of MB.
124	
125	---
126	
127	## 3. How to cut a mobile release
128	
129	For the native Xcode build and direct App Store Connect upload used by the
130	GitHub-hosted macOS runner, see
131	[MOBILE_TESTFLIGHT_GITHUB_ACTIONS_NATIVE.md](./MOBILE_TESTFLIGHT_GITHUB_ACTIONS_NATIVE.md).
132	
133	```bash
134	git checkout main && git pull
135	git tag mobile-v0.2.0
136	git push origin mobile-v0.2.0
137	```
138	
139	CI ([`.github/workflows/mobile-testflight.yml`](../.github/workflows/mobile-testflight.yml)):
140	
141	1. creates a metadata-only GitHub Release without changing the desktop Latest,
142	2. runs on a macOS runner,
143	3. generates the iOS UniFFI/native module from `packages/mobile-core`,
144	4. archives and exports an `.ipa` with Xcode, and
145	5. validates and uploads that `.ipa` directly to App Store Connect/TestFlight.
146	
147	The workflow sets `MOBILE_VERSION` from the tag and uses the GitHub run number
148	as `IOS_BUILD_NUMBER`. For a manual rerun, use Actions → **Mobile TestFlight**
149	and optionally enter an explicit build number. Manual dispatch uploads a new
150	TestFlight build but does not create a GitHub Release; the `github-release` job
151	runs only for a pushed `mobile-v*` tag. A GitHub Release is version/tag-level,
152	not one-per-TestFlight-build-number.
153	
154	---
155	
156	## 4. Required GitHub secrets
157	
158	Add under **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**.
159

161	
162	The `ios` job uses the `testflight` GitHub Environment. Add the following as
163	environment secrets (or repository secrets if environment scoping is not

169	| `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID` | Team App Store Connect API key ID |
170	| `APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID` | Team App Store Connect API issuer ID |
171	| `APP_STORE_CONNECT_PRIVATE_KEY` | Complete contents of the API key `.p8` file |
172

177	See [MOBILE_TESTFLIGHT_GITHUB_ACTIONS_NATIVE.md](./MOBILE_TESTFLIGHT_GITHUB_ACTIONS_NATIVE.md)
